description: mstack's own work queue. The plugin runs on the harness it ships, which is the only way an unused workflow gets found out.
verify: npm test && npm run typecheck && bin/mstack lint-plugin .

items.title: Ship a statusline that renders the active item
acceptance: `mstack statusline` reads the stdin payload and prints one line
It shows the active item, its status, and the branch, and degrades to something useful when .mstack/ is absent
It never blocks a turn: any failure prints nothing and exits 0
README documents how a user wires it up, including that a plugin cannot register one on its own if that turns out to be true
items.description: The store already holds everything a statusline needs. Every turn currently shows the model and the cwd, and nothing about the work.
items.closed_by: Review panel: 4 reviewers, all CHANGES_REQUESTED, every finding reproduced and fixed with a mutation-verified test

items.title: Decide whether mstack can ship a subagentStatusLine at all
acceptance: Establish, with evidence rather than inference, whether the plugin's bin/ is on PATH for the subagent status line process
Establish whether ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is expanded in a plugin settings.json
Either ship settings.json with a command proven to resolve, or record why it cannot be shipped and close the item
items.description: A plugin may ship subagentStatusLine in its own settings.json, but nothing documents how that command would name mstack's own script.
items.decision_required: The substitution table in the plugins reference lists skills, agents, hooks, monitors, MCP and LSP, and settings.json is not among them. bin/ is documented as reaching the Bash tool only. Both mechanisms may still work and simply be undocumented, but relying on undocumented behaviour in the one plugin whose subject is evidence is its own decision.

items.title: Port the source playbooks the why half of understand lost
acceptance: understand carries per-source guidance for the sources a team actually has, as references rather than skills
Each one says what that source is good for and what it systematically lies about
The 1% skill listing budget is unaffected, so they stay out of skills/
items.description: pstack ships eight playbooks for reading a source: Slack, Linear, Notion, Sentry, Datadog and the rest. Merging how and why into one skill dropped them.
items.closed_by: Closed on the fact-check's findings being fixed

items.title: Give fan-out the tooling its prose already assumes
acceptance: A run id is allocated per fan-out so parallel workers cannot collide on a filename
The concurrency cap is enforced by code rather than mentioned in prose
A worker that returns without a report is reported by name, not as a count
Tests cover the collision the review panel already hit in the first end-to-end run
items.description: design and review both say launch in parallel and both name the twenty-subagent cap. Nothing enforces the cap, allocates run ids, or notices a worker that dropped out.
items.source: gap list, 2026-08-19; the review panel filename collision found on 2026-08-19
items.closed_by: Closed on the adversarial review's findings being fixed

items.title: Make decision_required a gate, not an announcement
acceptance: The gate refuses to let an item with decision_required reach a status past in_progress until the fork is answered
There is a recorded way to answer it that links the answer to the item, not a free-floating decisions.tsv row
An unanswered fork is named in the failure, quoting the question
Tests cover the refusal, the answer, and the fact that an item without the field is unaffected
items.description: An item can carry an unresolved product fork and reach done with nobody answering it. The gate's only mention of the field is inside a comment.
items.closed_by: Closed on the panel's findings being fixed, not on an approval

items.title: A typo'd flag must not kill the status bar
acceptance: Any unparseable argument to statusline still exits 0 with nothing on stderr
The behaviour is the same for the subagent path
Other subcommands keep their strict parsing, because there a typo should be loud
items.description: mstack statusline --subagents exits 2 and writes to stderr. Same broken promise as the EPIPE, through a different door.
items.closed_by: Closed on the panel's findings being fixed

items.title: Drive the spec path to done, not just into it
acceptance: The example's sdd item reaches done through spec, spec-review, implement, verify and review
The four spec artifacts exist and are not stubs
Whatever the run breaks is fixed or recorded, the way the first three runs were
items.description: export-json sits at specifying with an empty specs directory. The direct path ran twice; the SDD half is verified only as far as entering it.
items.closed_by: Verified by an independent headless run, not by the session that asked for it

items.title: Cut 0.1.0
acceptance: The changelog entry matches what shipped, with the real test count
An annotated tag exists at the commit that is 0.1.0
README install instructions work against a clean clone
items.description: Both manifests say 0.1.0 and nothing is tagged.

items.title: README and wiki that teach mstack to a stranger
acceptance: A first-time reader goes from clone to a first closed item by following the README in order; every command block is copy-pasteable and its output shown from a real run
Credit to Lauren Tan (poteto) and the pstack lineage is visible in the README opening, and the full harness-meets-pstack story has its own wiki page

docs/wiki/ holds Home, Getting-Started, The-Story, How-A-Work-Item-Flows, Gates-and-Hooks, The-CLI, State-Files, Status-Line, Publishing-the-Wiki, _Sidebar and _Footer; every technical claim traces to the research doc, the code, or an official doc
Every relative link in README.md and docs/wiki resolves; Publishing-the-Wiki documents the exact route from these files to a live GitHub wiki
No claim a fact-check round verified is weakened or contradicted, and the CHANGELOG records the docs round under Unreleased
items.description: The README explains mstack to someone who already knows the story. Publication needs the reverse: a step-by-step on-ramp, the pstack and harness lineage with credit to poteto, and a wiki that exists as reviewable files before the GitHub repository does.
items.verification: npm test && npm run typecheck && bin/mstack lint-plugin . && node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs README.md docs/wiki/*.md
items.closed_by: Closed on the panel's 25 findings being fixed: reader and facts lenses, then a facts follow-up that re-verified 24 of 25 and specified the last two one-word fixes

items.title: The prose the panel flagged but item 9 could not touch
acceptance: Every mstack-authored claim about what a parent sees of a subagent matches the sub-agents docs: the working context is what it never sees, the final reply comes back, and 'a reply is not evidence' survives in every file that carried it
README, Gates-and-Hooks and The-Story characterise the shape-check defect with one formulation: shipped in production, pinned by the gate's comment to two of the harness's issue numbers
The four lines the round-2 sweep named as past the ~100-column convention are rewrapped: The-Story.md:49 and :59, Home.md:9, State-Files.md:5
docs/research/pstack-port.md and every quoted primary source stay byte-identical: they are records, not claims
The verification field runs green and the CHANGELOG Unreleased section records the round
items.description: Two follow-ups recorded in history.md at item 9's close: the reply-body phrasing in the five agent contracts and the router contradicts the sub-agents docs, and three pages characterise the shape-check defect two different ways. Plus the four reflow lines the round-2 sweep named.
